previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted with severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the right upper quadrant and back. Initial concern for peritonitis was ruled out by peritoneal fluid analysis showing no infection. Imaging showed no abscess or obstruction. Elevated liver enzymes and a history of medication use pointed to a toxic liver injury from statin and fibrate therapy, which were discontinued. The patient also experienced difficulty draining his peritoneal dialysis catheter, requiring two days of hemodialysis and a successful wire clearance procedure. His pain resolved, labs improved, and he was discharged home with adjusted insulin therapy and close follow-up planned.
problems: Mechanical complication due to peritoneal dialysis catheter
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Antilipemic and antiarteriosclerotic drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with h/o ESRD on PD, CAD, systolic CHF, DM2 presents 
with dyspnea concerning for fluid overload.  

# Dyspnea: 
Felt to be consistent with pulmonary edema due to fluid overload 
in setting of ESRD with inadequate peritoneal dialysis. Prior to 
admission, last peritoneal dialysis session at 5 am ___. 
Patient recieved one cycle of peritoneal dialysis with no relief 
of symptoms overnight on ___. On ___ he underwent hemodialysis 
with removal of 4L of fluid. Patient improved substantially 
following this with clearing of crackles on exam and resolution 
of dyspnea and orthopnea. Oxygen saturation remained WNL 
throughout.
  
# ESRD on PD: 
Patient reported difficulty with peritoneal dialysis underlying 
his fluid retention. Prior to admission, last peritoneal 
dialysis session at 5 am ___. Patient recieved one cycle of 
peritoneal dialysis with no relief of symptoms overnight on 
___. On ___ he underwent hemodialysis with removal of 4L of 
fluid. Patient expressed frustrations with PD, such that the 
decision was made to hold PD in favor of HD until further 
evaluation. ___ revealed no change in catheter position, and 
sample of periotoneal fluid was not concerning for infection. 
Patient was discharged with same day appointment for HD. Furhter 
discussion regarding options for long term renal replacement 
therapy will be necessary in the outpatient setting. Patient was 
continued on home sevalamer, Nephrocaps, and cinacalcet. 

# Prolonged QT interval: 
ECG with prolonged QT (___), consistent with prior EKGs on 
review of records. Patient was monitored on telemetry with no 
significant arrhythmias. His Trazodone was discontinued given 
concern for QT prolongation. This should be discussed further in 
the outpatient setting.
    
# CAD: 
Patient with some chest discomfort with dyspnea on initial 
presentation. Given h/o CAD, concern for ACS. ECG was consistent 
with prior. Troponins were elevated, however CK-MB was normal 
and downtrending. Elevated troponins likely represent some 
demand ischemia in the setting of volume overload in addition to 
decreased renal clearance with ESRD. Patient's symptoms resolved 
following dialysis. He was continued on aspirin, lisinopril, 
carvedilol, and pravastatin.

# Congestive heart failure, systolic, acute on chronic:
See above. Continued carvedilol and lisinopril.

# DM2:
Continued home regimen of lantus and SSI.

# Hypertension:
Continued home isosorbide mononitrate, carvedilol and 
lisinopril. Patient was hyperkalemic on admission and treated 
with inadequate dialysis. He was treated with kayexelate with 
resolution. Lisinopril was continued and potassium remained 
stable with dialysis.

# Hyperlipidemia:
Continued pravastatin. LFTs were WNL.

# Depression: 
Not currently on medication. Patient noted to be overwhelmed 
with disease course and management overall but coping with 
family support. Further management deferred to outpatient 
setting.
